newsitem.title: CANADA: Goodale pledges to deal with grain shipment delays.
newsitem.headline: Goodale pledges to deal with grain shipment delays.

text.p: Canada's Agriculture Minister pledged Friday to study a proposal by grain handlers and shippers on how to avoid situations like this year's Pacific port backlog.

"The industry is working on a proposal right now that I would expect the government of Canada to receive in the weeks immediately ahead and it will obviously receive very careful consideration because our system must be more accountable, it must be more reliable," Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale told reporters on a conference call from Tokyo, where he is on a trade mission.
Four provincial ministers this week called for a federal inquiry into the Pacific port backlog which, at its worst, saw one ship berthed as long as 62 days at Vancouver.

"The railways and grain companies have proposed an industry led review of the situation. An inquiry or rewards and penalties are interesting ideas and useful and we'll take a very close look at them," Goodale said.
Heavy snow, extreme cold and equipment failure led to delays in rail shipments to Pacific ports since early January.
The Canadian Wheat Board faces more than C$15 million in demurrage fines and has deferred some sales.
